accepted.title: Real-analytic structure of absolute-period leaf closures
accepted.text: For g≥2 and a partition κ of 2g−2 into positive zero multiplicities, let Ω₁M_g(κ) be the area-one stratum of pairs (X,ω), where X is a closed genus-g Riemann surface and ω is a nonzero holomorphic one-form with zero multiplicities κ. Let A(κ) be the absolute period foliation: in local marked period coordinates its leaves keep all integrals of ω over closed integral cycles fixed. Let Per(ω)={∫_cω:c∈H₁(X;Z)}⊂C. For every leaf L of A(κ) in Ω₁M_g(κ), is its closure L̄ a properly immersed real-analytic suborbifold of Ω₁M_g(κ)?
accepted.subject: Geometry & Topology
accepted.citation: Question 1.6, held PDF physical p. 13, printed p. 5; definitions physical pp. 9–10, printed pp. 1–2.
accepted.scope_review: Read held PDF physical 9–14 (printed 1–6), including the assumptions of Theorems 1.1–1.5 and Questions 1.6–1.8. The questions concern every stratum and every leaf, without the connected-stratum and algebraically generic hypotheses of the preceding theorems. Closures are in the fixed area-one stratum, not in the entire Hodge bundle or in its compactification. SL(2,R) acts by postcomposing translation charts. No restriction to strata with at least two zeros is silently added; one-zero leaves are points and give elementary special cases.
accepted.duplicate_review: Full numbered catalog and corpus retrieval for absolute period/isoperiodic/leaf-closure/saturation terminology found no numbered equivalent or other extracted full-scope target. The three questions are related but differ: regularity of an individual closure, a specified orbit-saturation equality, and classification of all invariant saturated closed sets. Introductory generic open-question mentions carry no extra mathematical target.
accepted.literature_finding: June 2026 Winsor, Theorem 1.1 and introduction, gives a leaf-closure result outside an exceptional algebraic subset and explicitly describes further work as incomplete. This is relevant progress, not a theorem for all leaves in all strata. The 2022/2023 saturated-orbit paper classifies the full Hodge-bundle foliation, which allows zero collisions and differs from the stratum foliation here. No exact full closure was located in the dated primary scan.

accepted.title: Nonclosed absolute-period leaves with dense periods
accepted.text: For g≥2 and a partition κ of 2g−2 into positive zero multiplicities, let Ω₁M_g(κ) be the area-one stratum of pairs (X,ω), where X is a closed genus-g Riemann surface and ω is a nonzero holomorphic one-form with zero multiplicities κ. accepted.title: Closed invariant sets saturated for the absolute period foliation
accepted.text: For g≥2 and a partition κ of 2g−2 into positive zero multiplicities, let Ω₁M_g(κ) be the area-one stratum of pairs (X,ω), where X is a closed genus-g Riemann surface and ω is a nonzero holomorphic one-form with zero multiplicities κ.
